climate_note: As the Atlantic warms, the center of the summer flounder population has moved north along the East Coast, so more are now found off New England.
The Gulf of Maine is one of the fastest-warming ocean areas. Warmer water is linked to poorer survival of young cod, which makes recovery of the population harder.
Warming in the Gulf of Maine has moved the tiny copepods these whales eat, so the whales now spend more time in new areas such as Cape Cod Bay and the Gulf of St. Lawrence.
Milder winters let more green crabs survive, which has helped their numbers grow in New England and spread along the Pacific coast.
Lionfish cannot survive cold winter water. As winters warm, they may be able to live farther north along the Atlantic coast.
Snook die in cold snaps. With fewer hard freezes, their range has been spreading farther north along Florida's coasts.
source: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission
